name: What puts the present verb in naṣb or jazm
definition: The particles that take the muḍāriʿ out of its rafʿ: ten put it in naṣb, eighteen in jazm (al-Ājurrūmiyya).
body: The muḍāriʿ is in rafʿ until something comes upon it. The nawāṣib: an, lan, idhan, kay, the lām of kay, the lām of denial, ḥattā, and the answer with fa, wa and aw. The jawāzim: lam, lammā, a-lam, a-lammā, the lām of command, lā of prohibition, and the conditional words in, mā, man, mahmā, idhmā, ayy, matā, ayyāna, ayna, annā, ḥaythumā, kayfamā (and idhā in poetry).
In naṣb the singular verb takes fatḥa (lan yaḍriba); in jazm it takes sukūn (lam yaḍrib); the verbs ending in -āni, -ūna, -īna lose their nūn in both.
